thread:
alana: Quick sync — we need a lightweight plan for post-launch follow-ons. Customers are asking about reliability fixes + a couple UX asks. Can we agree a target split and owners for the next mini-cycle? :eyes:

mike: +1. What are the numbers right now? How many high-sev bugs vs quick wins?

jasmin: From QA/monitoring: 9 P1/P1.5 regressions (latency, streaming drops), ~18 medium bugs, and ~12 small UX polish asks. Also seeing 3 customer-blocking reports in support.

omar: Adding those 3 customers — two are on Dedicated plans, one is high ARR. They want an ETA on fixes.

alana: Propose a "staircase" approach: 
- Step 1 (hot lane): fix the 3 customer-blocking and top 2 P1s this week (TTR 48h)
- Step 2 (stability sprint): dedicate 60% of eng capacity next 2 weeks to remaining high/medium bugs
- Step 3 (polish lane): reserve 40% capacity for quick UX wins + 1-day patches
This aims to protect SLAs while shipping visible polish. Thoughts?

rachel: I like the parallel lanes. Design can bundle the UX asks into 3 quick PRs for review. Speed ok if scope is tiny.

mike: Capacity check — if we commit 60% of eng to stability, we need a plan for ongoing infra work. Can we run a small oncall rotation to handle infra without derailing fixes?

jasmin: We can set a two-person core for stability, other two handle infra/oncall. If more P1s surface, we escalate to the hot lane.

alana: Good. Criteria to promote a bug into hot lane: customer-blocking OR error rate > 1% AND reproducible with a short trace. Anything else?

omar: Also include any Dedicated-customer incidents as auto-promote.

product-bot: Deploy reminder: canary of the quick patch happens at 18:00 PST today.

alana: Action items: 
- mike -> triage and assign the hot lane today (owner + ETA)
- jasmin -> schedule stability sprint and publish capacity plan by EOD
- rachel -> bundle UX asks into 3 PRs by tomorrow noon
- omar -> notify the 3 customers with proposed TTRs and offer hotfix channel
Please add blockers here. :thumbsup:

mike: Will do. I’ll post the hot-lane owners in thread by 10:30.

jasmin: Scheduling note — recommend we treat any regression tied to streaming/KV cache as high priority; they cause most user impact.

alana: Agreed. If we keep the staircase cadence, we can aim to close top 12 bugs and ship 6 quick wins in the 2-week window. If anything blocks scope we re-evaluate mid-sprint.

omar: Sending initial customer messages now.

rachel: PRs will be ready for review tomorrow.

mike: Hot-lane owners posted: @jasmin (streaming), @leo (latency), @maya (customer Dedicated fixes).

alana: Thanks — closing this sync. We’ll reconvene Friday 16:00 PT for mid-sprint check.

product-bot: Reminder set for Friday 16:00 PT — #product.
